name: Covered Call
setup: You own the stock; Sell a call, strike price A; Generally, the stock price will be below strike A
when: You’re neutral to bullish, and you’re willing to sell stock if it reaches a specific price.
breakeven: Current stock price minus the premium received for selling the call.
max_profit: When the call is first sold, potential profit is limited to the strike price minus the current stock price plus the premium received for selling the call.
max_loss: … (see source)
margin: Because you own the stock, no additional margin is required.

name: Protective Put
setup: You own the stock; Buy a put, strike price A; Generally, the stock price will be above strike A
when: You’re bullish but nervous.
breakeven: From the point the protective put is established, the break-even point is the current stock price plus the premium paid for the put.
max_profit: Potential profit is theoretically unlimited, because you’ll still own the stock and you have not capped the upside.
max_loss: Risk is limited to the “deductible” plus the premium paid for the put.
margin: After the trade is paid for, no additional margin is required.

name: Collar
setup: You own the stock; Buy a put, strike price A; Sell a call, strike price B; Generally, the stock price will be between strikes Aand B
when: You’re bullish but nervous.
breakeven: From the point the collar is established, there are two break-even points: If established for a net credit, the break-even is current stock price minus net credit received. … (see source)
max_profit: From the point the collar is established, potential profit is limited to strike B minus current stock price minus the net debit paid, or plus net credit received.
max_loss: From the point the collar is established, risk is limited to the current stock price minus strike A plus the net debit paid, or minus the net credit received.
margin: Because you own the stock, the call you sold is considered “covered.” So no additional margin is required after the trade is established.

name: Cash-Secured Put
setup: Sell a put, strike price A; Keep enough cash on hand to buy the stock if the put is assigned; Generally, the stock price will be above strike A
when: You’re slightly bearish short-term, bullish long-term.
breakeven: Strike A minus the premium received for the put.
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to the premium received from selling the put.
max_loss: Potential loss is substantial, but limited to the strike price if the stock goes to zero.
margin: You must have enough cash to cover the cost of purchasing the stock at the strike price.

name: Long Call
setup: Buy a call, strike price A; Generally, the stock price will be at or above strike A
when: You’re bullish as a matador.
breakeven: Strike A plus the cost of the call.
max_profit: There’s a theoretically unlimited profit potential, if the stock goes to infinity.
max_loss: Risk is limited to the premium paid for the call option.
margin: After the trade is paid for, no additional margin is required.

name: Long Put
setup: Buy a put, strike price A; Generally, the stock price will be at or below strike A
when: You’re bearish as a grizzly.
breakeven: Strike A minus the cost of the put.
max_profit: There’s a substantial profit potential. If the stock goes to zero you make the entire strike price minus the cost of the put contract.
max_loss: Risk is limited to the premium paid for the put.
margin: After the trade is paid for, no additional margin is required.

name: Fig Leaf
setup: Buy an in-the-money LEAPS call, strike price A; Sell an out-of-the-money short-term call, strike price B; Generally, the stock price will be closer to strike B than strike A
when: You’re mildly bullish
breakeven: It is possible to approximate break-even points, but there are too many variables to give an exact formula. … (see source)
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to the premium received for sale of the front-month call plus the performance of the LEAPS call.
max_loss: Potential risk is limited to the debit paid to establish the strategy.
margin: After the trade is paid for, no additional margin is required.

name: Long Call Spread
setup: Buy a call, strike price A; Sell a call, strike price B; Generally, the stock will be at or above strike A and below strike B
when: You’re bullish, but you have an upside target.
breakeven: Strike A plus net debit paid.
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to the difference between strike A and strike B minus the net debit paid.
max_loss: Risk is limited to the net debit paid.
margin: After the trade is paid for, no additional margin is required.

name: Long Put Spread
setup: Sell a put, strike price A; Buy a put, strike price B; Generally, the stock will be at or below strike B and above strike A
when: You’re bearish, with a downside target.
breakeven: Strike B minus the net debit paid.
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to the difference between strike A and strike B, minus the net debit paid.
max_loss: Risk is limited to the net debit paid.
margin: After the trade is paid for, no additional margin is required.

name: Short Call Spread
setup: Sell a call, strike price A; Buy a call, strike price B; Generally, the stock will be below strike A
when: You’re bearish. You may also be expecting neutral activity if strike A is out-of-the-money.
breakeven: Strike A plus the net credit received when opening the position.
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to the net credit received when opening the position.
max_loss: Risk is limited to the difference between strike A and strike B, minus the net credit received.
margin: Margin requirement is the difference between the strike prices.

name: Short Put Spread
setup: Buy a put, strike price A; Sell a put, strike price B; Generally, the stock will be above strike B
when: You're bullish. You may also be anticipating neutral activity if strike B is out-of-the-money.
breakeven: Strike B minus the net credit received when selling thespread.
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to the net credit you receive when you set up the strategy.
max_loss: Risk is limited to the difference between strike A andstrike B, minus the net credit received.
margin: Margin requirement is the difference between the strike prices.

name: Long Straddle
setup: Buy a call, strike price A; Buy a put, strike price A; Generally, the stock price will be at strike A
when: You’re anticipating a swing in stock price, but you’re not sure which direction it will go.
breakeven: There are two break-even points: Strike A plus the net debit paid.; Strike A minus the net debit paid.
max_profit: Potential profit is theoretically unlimited if the stock goes up.; If the stock goes down, potential profit may be substantial but limited to the strike price minus the net debit paid.
max_loss: Potential losses are limited to the net debit paid.
margin: After the trade is paid for, no additional margin is required.

name: Long Strangle
setup: Buy a put, strike price A; Buy a call, strike price B; Generally, the stock price will be between strikes A and B
when: You’re anticipating a swing in stock price, but you’re not sure which direction it will go.
breakeven: There are two break-even points: Strike A minus the net debit paid.; Strike B plus the net debit paid.
max_profit: Potential profit is theoretically unlimited if the stock goes up.; If the stock goes down, potential profit may be substantial but limited to strike A minus the net debit paid.
max_loss: Potential losses are limited to the net debit paid.
margin: After the trade is paid for, no additional margin is required.

name: Back Spread w/Calls
setup: Sell a call, strike price A; Buy two calls, strike price B; Generally, the stock will be at or around strike price A
when: You’re extremely bullish on a highly volatile stock.
breakeven: If established for a net debit, the break-even point is equal to strike B plus the maximum risk.; If established for a net credit, there are two break-even points for this play: Strike A plus the net credit received … (see source)
max_profit: There’s a theoretically unlimited profit potential if the stock goes to infinity. But since the real world doesn’t always operate like a theoretical one, let’s just say “a lot.”
max_loss: Risk is limited to strike B minus strike A, minus the net credit received or plus the net debit paid.
margin: Margin requirement is the difference between the strike prices of the short call spread embedded into this strategy.

name: Back Spread w/Puts
setup: Sell a put, strike price B; Buy two puts, strike price A; Generally, the stock will be at or around strike price B
when: You’re extremely bearish on a highly volatile stock.
breakeven: If established for a net debit, the break-even point is strike A minus the maximum risk.; If established for a net credit, there are two break-even points for this play: Strike A minus the maximum risk … (see source)
max_profit: There is a substantial profit potential if the stock goes to zero. But keep in mind stocks don’t go to zero very often.
max_loss: Risk is limited to strike B minus strike A, minus the net credit received or plus the net debit paid.
margin: Margin requirement is the difference between the strike prices of the short put spread embedded into this strategy.

name: Long Calendar Spread w/Calls
setup: Sell a call, strike price A; Buy a call, strike price A; Generally, the stock will be at or around strike A
when: You’re anticipating minimal movement on the stock within a specific time frame.
breakeven: It is possible to approximate break-even points, but there are too many variables to give an exact formula. … (see source)
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to the premium received for the back-month call minus the cost to buy back the front-month call, minus the net debit paid to establish the position.
max_loss: Limited to the net debit paid to establish the trade.
margin: After the trade is paid for, no additional margin isrequired if the position is closed at expiration of the front-month option.

name: Long Calendar Spread w/Puts
setup: Sell a put, strike price A; Buy a put, strike price A; Generally, the stock will be at or around strike A
when: You’re anticipating minimal movement on the stock within a specific time frame.
breakeven: It is possible to approximate break-even points, but there are too many variables to give an exact formula. … (see source)
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to the premium received for the back-month put minus the cost to buy back the front-month put, minus the net debit paid to establish the position.
max_loss: Limited to the net debit paid to establish the trade.
margin: After the trade is paid for, no additional margin is required if the position is closed at expiration of the front-month option.

name: Diagonal Spread w/Calls
setup: Sell an out-of-the-money call, strike price A; Buy a further out-of-the-money call, strike price B; At expiration of the front-month call, sell another call with strike A and the same expiration as the back-month call … (see source)
when: You’re expecting neutral activity during the front month, then neutral to bearish activity during the back month.
breakeven: It is possible to approximate break-even points, but there are too many variables to give an exact formula. … (see source)
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to the net credit received for selling both calls with strike A, minus the premium paid for the call with strike B.
max_loss: If established for a net credit, risk is limited to the difference between strike A and strike B, minus the net credit received. … (see source)
margin: Margin requirement is the difference between the strike prices.

name: Diagonal Spread w/Puts
setup: Sell an out-of-the-money put, strike price B; Buy a further out-of-the-money put, strike price A; At expiration of the front-month put, sell another put with strike B and the same expiration as the back-month put … (see source)
when: You’re expecting neutral activity during the front month, then neutral to bullish activity during the back month.
breakeven: It is possible to approximate break-even points, but there are too many variables to give an exact formula. … (see source)
max_profit: Profit is limited to the net credit received for selling bothputs with strike B, minus the premium paid for the putwith strike A.
max_loss: If established for a net credit, risk is limited to the difference between strike A and strike B, minus the net credit received. … (see source)
margin: Margin requirement is the difference between the strike prices.

name: Long Butterfly w/Calls
setup: Buy a call, strike price A; Sell two calls, strike price B; Buy a call, strike price C; Generally, the stock will be at strike B
when: Typically, investors will use butterfly spreads when anticipating minimal movement on the stock within a specific time frame.
breakeven: There are two break-even points for this play: Strike A plus the net debit paid.; Strike C minus the net debit paid.
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to strike B minus strike A minus the net debit paid.
max_loss: Risk is limited to the net debit paid.
margin: After the trade is paid for, no additional margin is required.

name: Long Butterfly w/Puts
setup: Buy a put, strike price A; Sell two puts, strike price B; Buy a put, strike price C; Generally, the stock will be at strike B
when: Typically, investors will use butterfly spreads when anticipating minimal movement on the stock within a specific time frame.
breakeven: There are two break-even points for this play: Strike A plus the net debit paid.; Strike C minus the net debit paid.
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to strike C minus strike B minus the net debit paid.
max_loss: Risk is limited to the net debit paid.
margin: After the trade is paid for, no additional margin is required.

name: Iron Butterfly
setup: Buy a put, strike price A; Sell a put, strike price B; Sell a call, strike price B; Buy a call, strike price C; Generally, the stock will be at strike B
when: Typically, investors will use butterfly spreads when anticipating minimal movement on the stock within a specific time frame.
breakeven: There are two break-even points for this play: Strike B plus net credit received.; Strike B minus net credit received.
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to the net credit received.
max_loss: Risk is limited to strike B minus strike A, minus the net credit received when establishing the position.
margin: Margin requirement is the short call spread requirement or short put spread requirement.

name: Skip Strike Butterfly w/Calls
setup: Buy a call, strike price A; Sell two calls, strike price B; Skip over strike price C; Buy a call, strike price D; Generally, the stock will be at or below strike A
when: You’re slightly bullish. You want the stock to rise to strike B and then stop.
breakeven: If established for a net credit then the break-even point is strike C plus the net credit received when establishing the strategy.; If established for a net debit, then there are two break-even points: Strike A plus net debit paid. … (see source)
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to strike B minus strike A minus the net debit paid, or plus the net credit received.
max_loss: Risk is limited to the difference between strike C and strike D minus the net credit received or plus the net debit paid.
margin: Margin requirement is equal to the difference between the strike prices of the short call spread embedded into this strategy.

name: Skip Strike Butterfly w/Puts
setup: Buy a put, strike price A; Skip strike price B; Sell two puts, strike price C; Buy a put, strike price D; Generally, the stock will be at or above strike D
when: You’re slightly bearish. You want the stock to go down to strike C and then stop.
breakeven: If established for a net credit then the break-even point is strike B minus the net credit received when establishing the strategy.; If established for a net debit, then there are two break-even points: Strike D minus net debit paid. … (see source)
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to strike D minus strike C minus the net debit paid, or plus the net credit received.
max_loss: Risk is limited to the difference between strike A and strike B, minus the net credit received or plus the net debit paid.
margin: Margin requirement is equal to the difference between the strike prices of the short put spread embedded into this strategy.

name: Inverse Skip Strike Butterfly w/Calls
setup: Sell a call with strike price A; Buy two calls with strike price B; Skip over strike price C; Sell a call with strike price D; Generally, the stock will be at or around strike price A
when: You’re extremely bullish on a highly volatile stock.
breakeven: If established for a net debit, the break-even point is strike C plus the net debit paid.; If established for a net credit, there are two break-even points: Strike A plus the net credit received … (see source)
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to strike D minus strike C minus the net debit paid, or plus the net credit received.
max_loss: Potential risk is limited to strike B minus strike A plus the net debit paid, or minus the net credit received.
margin: Margin requirement is equal to the difference between the strike prices of the short call spread embedded into this strategy.

name: Inverse Skip Strike Butterfly w/Puts
setup: Sell a put with strike price D; Buy two puts with strike price C; Skip over strike price B; Sell a put with strike price A; Generally, the stock will be at or around strike price D
when: You’re extremely bearish on a highly volatile stock.
breakeven: If established for a net debit, the break-even point is strike B minus the net debit paid.; If established for a net credit, there are two break-even points: Strike D minus the net credit received … (see source)
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to strike B minus strike A minus the net debit paid, or plus the net credit received.
max_loss: Potential risk is limited to strike D minus strike C plus the net debit paid, or minus the net credit received.
margin: Margin requirement is equal to the difference between the strike prices of the short put spread embedded into this strategy.

name: Christmas Tree Butterfly w/Calls
setup: Buy a call, strike price A; Skip over strike price B; Sell three calls, strike price C; Buy two calls, strike price D; Generally, the stock will be at or around strike A
when: You’re slightly bullish. You want the stock to rise to strike C and then stop.
breakeven: There are two break-even points for this strategy: Strike A plus the net debit paid; Strike D minus one-half of the net debit paid
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to strike C minus strike A minus the net debit paid.
max_loss: Risk is limited to the net debit paid.
margin: After the trade is paid for, no additional margin is required.

name: Christmas Tree Butterfly w/Puts
setup: Buy a put, strike price D; Skip over strike price C; Sell three puts, strike price B; Buy two puts, strike price A; Generally, the stock will be at or around strike D
when: You’re slightly bearish. You want the stock to fall to strike B and then stop.
breakeven: There are two break-even points for this strategy: Strike D minus the net debit paid; Strike A plus half the net debit paid
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to strike D minus strike B minus the net debit paid.
max_loss: Risk is limited to the net debit paid.
margin: After the trade is paid for, no additional margin is required.

name: Long Condor Spread w/Calls
setup: Buy a call, strike price A; Sell a call, strike price B; Sell a call, strike price C; Buy a call, strike price D; Generally, the stock will be between strike price Band strike price C
when: You’re anticipating minimal movement on the stock within a specific time frame.
breakeven: There are two break-even points: Strike A plus the net debit paid; Strike D minus the net debit paid
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to strike B minus strike A minus the net debit paid.
max_loss: Risk is limited to the net debit paid to establish the condor.
margin: After the trade is paid for, no additional margin is required.

name: Long Condor Spread w/Puts
setup: Buy a put, strike price A; Sell a put, strike price B; Sell a put, strike price C; Buy a put, strike price D; Generally, the stock will be between strike price Band strike price C
when: You’re anticipating minimal movement on the stock within a specific time frame.
breakeven: There are two break-even points: Strike A plus the net debit paid; Strike D minus the net debit paid
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to strike D minus strike C minusthe net debit paid.
max_loss: Risk is limited to the net debit paid to establish the condor.
margin: After the trade is paid for, no additional margin is required.

name: Iron Condor
setup: Buy a put, strike A; Sell a put, strike B; Sell a call, strike C; Buy a call, strike D; Generally, the stock will be between strike price Band strike price C
when: You’re anticipating minimal movement on the stock within a specific time frame.
breakeven: There are two break-even points: Strike B minus the net credit received.; Strike C plus the net credit received.
max_profit: Profit is limited to the net credit received.
max_loss: Risk is limited to strike B minus strike A, minus the netcredit received.
margin: Margin requirement is the short call spread requirement or short put spread requirement.

name: Short Call
setup: Sell a call, strike price A; Generally, the stock price will be below strike A
when: You’re bearish to neutral.
breakeven: Strike A plus the premium received for the call.
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to the premium received for selling the call.; If the stock keeps rising above strike A, you keep losing money.
max_loss: Risk is theoretically unlimited. If the stock keeps rising, you keep losing money.
margin: Margin requirement is the greater of the following: 25% of the underlying security value minus the out-of-the-money amount, plus the premium received; OR 10% of the underlying security value plus the premium received

name: Short Put
setup: Sell a put, strike price A; Generally, the stock price will be above strike A
when: You’re bullish to neutral.
breakeven: Strike A minus the premium received for the put.
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to the premium received for selling the put.
max_loss: Potential loss is substantial, but limited to the strike price minus the premium received if the stock goes to zero.
margin: Margin requirement is the greater of the following: 25% of the underlying security value minus the out-of-the-money amount, plus the premium received; OR 10% of the underlying security value plus the premium received

name: Short Straddle
setup: Sell a call, strike price A; Sell a put, strike price A; Generally, the stock price will be at strike A
when: You’re expecting minimal movement on the stock.
breakeven: There are two break-even points: Strike A minus the net credit received.; Strike A plus the net credit received.
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to the net credit received for selling the call and the put.
max_loss: If the stock goes up, your losses could be theoretically unlimited.; If the stock goes down, your losses may be substantial but limited to the strike price minus net credit received for selling the straddle.
margin: Margin requirement is the short call or short put requirement, plus the premium received from the other side.

name: Short Strangle
setup: Sell a put, strike price A; Sell a call, strike price B; Generally, the stock price will be between strikes Aand B
when: You are anticipating minimal movement on the stock.
breakeven: There are two break-even points: Strike A minus the net credit received.; Strike B plus the net credit received.
max_profit: Potential profit is limited to the net credit received.
max_loss: If the stock goes up, your losses could be theoretically unlimited.; If the stock goes down, your losses may be substantia but limited to strike A minus the net credit received.
margin: Margin requirement is the short call or short put requirement, plus the premium received from the other side.

name: Long Combination
setup: Buy a call, strike price A; Sell a put, strike price A; The stock should be at or very near strike A
when: You’re bullish.
breakeven: Strike A plus the net debit paid or minus the net credit received to establish the strategy.
max_profit: There is a theoretically unlimited profit potential if the stock price keeps rising.
max_loss: Potential loss is substantial, but limited to strike price A plus the net debit paid or minus net credit received.
margin: Margin requirement is the short put requirement.

name: Short Combination
setup: Sell a call, strike price A; Buy a put, strike price A; The stock should be at or very near strike A
when: You’re bearish.
breakeven: Strike A plus the net credit received or minus the net debit paid to establish the strategy.
max_profit: Potential profit is substantial if stock goes to zero, but limited to strike price A plus the net credit received or minus the net debit paid to establish the strategy.
max_loss: Risk is theoretically unlimited if the stock price keeps rising.
margin: Margin requirement is the short call requirement.

name: Front Spread w/Calls
setup: Buy a call, strike price A; Sell two calls, strike price B; Generally, the stock will be below or at strike A
when: You’re slightly bullish. You want the stock to rise to strike B and then stop.
breakeven: If established for a net debit, there are two break-even points: Strike A plus net debit paid to establish the position.; Strike B plus the maximum profit potential.; If established for a net credit, there is only one break-even point: … (see source)
max_profit: If established for a net debit, potential profit is limited to the difference between strike A and strike B, minus the net debit paid. … (see source)
max_loss: If established for a net debit: Risk is limited to the debit paid for the spread if the stock price goes down.; Risk is unlimited if the stock price goes way, way up.; If established for a net credit: … (see source)
margin: Margin requirement is the requirement for the uncovered short call portion of the front spread.

name: Front Spread w/Puts
setup: Sell two puts, strike price A; Buy a put, strike price B; Generally, the stock will be at or above strike B.
when: You’re slightly bearish. You want the stock to go down to strike A and then stop.
breakeven: If established for a net debit, there are two break-even points: Strike B minus the net debit paid to establish the position.; Strike A minus the maximum profit potential. … (see source)
max_profit: If established for a net debit, potential profit is limited to the difference between strike A and strike B, minus the net debit paid. … (see source)
max_loss: If established for a net debit: Risk is limited to the net debit paid if the stock price goes up.; Risk is substantial but limited to strike A plus the net debit paid if the stock goes to zero. … (see source)
margin: Margin requirement is the requirement for the uncovered short put portion of the front spread.

name: Double Diagonal
setup: Buy an out-of-the-money put, strike price A; Sell an out-of-the-money put, strike price B; Sell an out-of-the-money call, strike price C; Buy an out-of-the-money call, strike price D … (see source)
when: You’re anticipating minimal movement on the stock over at least two option expiration cycles.
breakeven: It is possible to approximate your break-even points, but there are too many variables to give an exact formula. … (see source)
max_profit: … (see source)
max_loss: … (see source)
margin: Margin requirement is the diagonal call spread requirement or the diagonal put spread requirement.
